{{NAME_1}}.role: a student of Grade 5 who has two chocolates of different sizes and says 1/3 of one is bigger than 1/2 of the other (the book says 'she')

{{NAME_2}}.role: plays with his fraction kit and makes a whole with pieces of 1/2 and 1/4 (the book says 'his')

{{NAME_3}}.role: shades one-third of figures and draws horizontal lines to make more equal parts (the book says 'He')

{{NAME_4}}.role: ate 1/3 of the chikki and compares paratha fractions with Shami; the book gives no pronoun

{{NAME_5}}.role: ate the rest of the chikki, 2/3, and compares paratha fractions with Sevi; the book gives no pronoun

{{NAME_6}}.role: child of the family whose father makes parathas; eats and counts pieces; shares the pizza (the book says 'he')

{{NAME_7}}.role: Raman's sister; takes 6 halves of paratha and receives a slice of pizza (the book says 'sister')

_note_kin: Maa, Baba, Dadiji, Dadaji and Raman's father are the family members of the book; they are kin words, not names, so they have no token. Write them as the book does (Maa, Baba, Dadiji, Dadaji, Raman's father).
